person.name: Joel Hibbard
person.headline: Technology leader who drives enterprise-scale adoption and builds modern platforms end to end

summary: Technology and operations leader with 30+ years in high-stakes environments: military medicine, the operating room, DoD security programs and global enterprise systems. My current work shows two sides of the same capability. At BCD Travel I lead enterprise adoption, moving a global operations platform off legacy Power Apps / SharePoint onto a governed, secure PostgreSQL stack that teams actually use. As the founder of Inpsyght, I build a behavioral-health platform on a modern cloud stack (Supabase, row-level security, serverless TypeScript, Stripe) with privacy and consent engineered in from day one. A clinical-psychology lens shapes how I design for behavior, communicate with executives and bring skeptical teams along.

value_props.title: Enterprise adoption at scale
value_props.text: At BCD Travel: moved a 48-screen Power Apps / SharePoint platform onto ToolJet and AWS PostgreSQL. The work included tiered role-based access, a cutover and rollback plan, and the training that made the change stick.

value_props.title: Modern stack, built end to end
value_props.text: At Inpsyght: a two-sided health platform on Supabase with row-level security on every table, 120+ migrations, serverless TypeScript, Stripe billing, and consent and de-identification built in.

value_props.title: Designed around human behavior
value_props.text: Clinical-psychology training and decades of instructional design shape how I build. I study how people actually work, design for it, and ship guides and training with every release.

technical: TypeScript / Deno serverless functions, Stripe billing

skill_bridges.evidence: Phased Power Apps → ToolJet/PostgreSQL migration with a go-live runbook, success criteria and rollback.
Tiered access model with a restricted fence for government accounts; least-privilege DB users; SSO.
Versioned consent, guardian safeguards for minors, de-identified research data and account purge, all built into the Inpsyght platform.
Inpsyght's emotion and body-mapping model is built on clinical theory. The BCD React modules follow how operations staff actually look up policy, payment and traveler data.
User guides, GIF/video walkthroughs and release notes published alongside each release.
FMF Corpsman, surgical first assistant and ICS-certified. That experience carries over to production incidents and go-lives.

experience.title: Performance Solutions Manager — Learning Tools & Platform Development
experience.context: Enterprise adoption: a global corporate travel management company. I lead the design and delivery of the internal operations platforms account and service teams rely on.

bullets.text: Led the modernization of the enterprise Account Tool. The legacy Power Apps canvas app (48 screens, ~60 SharePoint and Office 365 data sources) moved to a self-hosted ToolJet front end on AWS PostgreSQL, following a five-phase roadmap: UX, architecture, migration, security and cutover.

Designed the data model and multi-tenant access control: tiered Global, Regional, Country and Scoped access across a GCN → SMID → LCN account hierarchy, a restricted-access fence for government accounts, least-privilege database roles, TLS and SSO/OAuth2 user provisioning.

Engineered 11 custom React (JSX) components (~10K lines) covering policy, form of payment, travel bookers, passport and visa, country security risk, suppliers and fare rules. They replaced the custom logic that had lived in Power Apps.

Architected a SharePoint → object storage (S3/R2) → PostgreSQL knowledge pipeline. It uses Microsoft Graph delta change detection, converts Office documents to PDF, Markdown and AI-enriched JSON, prevents overlapping runs with lock files and reconciles its own inventory.

Defined release governance: migration-based schema control with CI/CD to staging, staging → dev → prod data-promotion scripts with duplicate detection and preload validation, and an hour-by-hour go-live plan with named owners, success criteria and rollback.
Drove adoption through performance-support content: user guides, GIF/video walkthroughs and release notes published to GitHub-hosted wikis and embedded in-app viewers.

Serve as the bridge between operations leadership and engineering. I translate business rules (payment, policy, approvals, vendor programs) into specifications, runbooks and stakeholder-ready design documents.

experience.title: Founder & Product Architect
experience.context: Modern-stack product build: a behavioral-health platform connecting client self-reflection with provider care. I own the product vision, the clinical model and the full backend.

bullets.text: Founded and am building a two-sided behavioral-health product. Clients capture emotions, body sensations and mindfulness practice. Providers on a subscription portal get client summaries, emotion timelines, standardized assessments such as the PHQ-9 and intervention-efficacy tracking.

Architected the Supabase / PostgreSQL backend: ~50 tables with row-level security on every one, 120+ versioned migrations, and server-side functions powering client dashboards, emotion-vector analytics, somatic heatmaps and provider reporting.

Engineered privacy and consent from the ground up: versioned legal documents with re-consent, a consent audit history, minimum-age rules for 113 jurisdictions, guardian safeguards for minors, provider license verification and automated account purge.

Built a de-identified research pipeline. Records are pseudonymized and the identity link is destroyed on account purge. It also has opt-in gating, a read-only research role and aggregate extracts with small-cell suppression.

Shipped Stripe subscription billing on Deno / TypeScript edge functions (checkout, webhooks, customer portal, billing notices). Provider access is tied to active billing, scheduled jobs run on pg_cron, and product telemetry is designed to exclude clinical content.

Translated clinical-psychology theory into the product's data model: emotion taxonomy with valence and dyads, locus of control, response-intention and agency scoring, and motivation trajectories. I also built a structured diagnostic-reference knowledge base for clinical context.
Directed learning management system (LMS) content delivery, virtual learning environments and the governance standards that applied across corporate agencies.
Led data integration across company platforms, writing use cases and process maps for development and engineering teams.
Built KPI and trend dashboards for senior-leadership monitoring and reporting.
Managed physical and logical access-control programs across multiple Department of Defense facilities, covering security operations and compliance training.
Advised senior stakeholders on access-control technology and programs of record. Built analytics that combined physical-security and ingress data to surface site-level trends.
Negotiated and executed contracts and renewals with DoD agencies, and represented the program to tenant sponsor communities.
Led implementation, training and evaluation for virtual tracking and monitoring systems, UAV systems and human-systems evaluation. Wrote SOPs and safety controls for trainers and role players.
Evaluated and targeted international oil-and-gas customers for monitoring-system adoption.
Founded and ran a training business offering threat-avoidance curriculum and scenario-based law-enforcement training. Built competency frameworks to evaluate individual performance.
Managed a $3.2M territory, providing surgical case coverage and patient device programming for neuromodulation and intrathecal drug-delivery therapies.
Ran regional and national physician training, resident education and speaker programs. Integrated practice-management tools for client practices.

earlier_career.text: Surgical First Assistant (travel and staff), 1998–2005: trauma, neuro, orthopedic and cardiac specialties nationwide.
U.S. Navy Hospital Corpsman, FMF, 1st Marine Division, 1991–1997 (Honorable Discharge). Combat casualty care training and medical readiness for rapid-deployment units.
